subtype_label: Focus internal / focus inference (no given focus)
query: Help me understand what's in these airline reviews — I'm not sure which aspect is most worth analyzing.

judge.implied_focus: Perceived airline experience quality — a qualitative, review-derived assessment of the flight across a few evaluative dimensions (crew/service, seat comfort, value, service reliability).

per_column.name: crew_professionalism_assessment
per_column.rationale: Qualitative categorization of staff conduct (exceptional/indifferent/rude/standard) — a clear service facet of the experience-quality framing, going beyond the numeric 'Staff Service' rating by naming behavioural modes.

per_column.name: seat_physical_comfort
per_column.rationale: Categorizes the physical seating experience (comfortable/adequate/cramped/broken) — a distinct comfort facet, adding a 'broken_defective' state absent from the numeric 'Seat Comfort' rating.

per_column.name: value_for_money_perception
per_column.rationale: Qualitative value judgement (poor/good/excellent/not_worth_premium) — a value facet, largely re-encoding the existing 'Value For Money' rating but with a premium-expectation nuance.

per_column.name: service_consistency_reliability
per_column.rationale: Assesses reliability/consistency of service (reliable/unpredictable/declining) — a service facet, but conceptually overlaps heavily with crew_professionalism, so it does not cleanly add an independent dimension.

judge.rationale: The four columns are not noise — they are all qualitative, text-inferable evaluative dimensions of the flying experience, so they share a broad theme of 'perceived airline experience quality.' However, the focus-inference mandate is to PROPOSE ONE coherent focus, and here the system instead spread across several top-level aspects (crew, seat, value, reliability) rather than committing to a single focus and decomposing IT. This reads more like a menu of candidate aspects — the very indecision the analyst expressed — than a sharply centred focus, so coherence is only moderate. Structurally the facets are useful in granularity (they add nuanced categories like 'broken_defective', 'declining', 'not_worth_premium'), but three of them (crew, seat, value) essentially re-encode existing numeric columns (Staff Service, Seat Comfort, Value For Money), and crew_professionalism vs service_consistency are near-duplicative on the service dimension, weakening the differentiation and novelty of the structure. The implied focus (experience/service quality) is genuinely actionable — an analyst could investigate its drivers and link to Overall Rating / Recommended — hence the higher actionability score, though it is somewhat blunted by the redundancy with pre-existing ratings.
